reflection.quote: Enough is as good as a feast.
reflection.reading:
Saturday in mid-October. The light comes in at that slant that only happens this time of year — low, honey-colored, gone by five. If you're newer to this, Saturdays can feel like the hardest shift. The whole week built toward a release valve, and now the valve doesn't work the way it used to. You're left with a day and no instructions.

I remember thinking sobriety would mean Saturdays got smaller. That I'd be the guy at home while everyone else was out living. What actually happened is the opposite. The Saturdays got bigger because I was in them. A morning walk where I actually noticed the trees turning. Coffee that tasted like coffee instead of a chaser for last night. A friend texting about dinner and me saying yes and meaning it. These aren't consolation prizes. They're the actual thing. The drinking was the consolation prize — a counterfeit version of a full day, bought on credit and paid for Sunday.

P.L. Travers wrote that enough is as good as a feast, and she was onto something. The trick isn't to make today exceptional. The trick is to let an ordinary Saturday be enough — to stop auditioning it against some other version of your life. You're here. The light is good. That's a lot.
reflection.meditation: Where in today could I let 'enough' actually be enough?

affirmations: I am building a life I don't need to escape from.
Today I can let an ordinary day be a good day.
I am present for the Saturday in front of me, not the one I think I should be having.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a quiet morning that didn't cost me anything. Grateful for the people who stayed when I was hard to be around, and the ones who showed up after I got honest. Grateful for a body that works, a day with nothing I have to hide, and the slow autumn light coming through the window.
gratitude.closing: One more day on the right side of it.
